args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest deploy) was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Rolled back to the most recent healthy production release, v2.3.0, in all regions. Incident opened to track investigation of the v2.3.1 regression.

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what I did:

## Actions taken

1. **Diagnosed the issue**
   - `checkout-api` was running **v2.3.1** (the latest deploy) in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with **unhealthy** status and an **18% error rate**.
   - Deployment history confirmed v2.3.1 was the only unhealthy production release; the most recent healthy production release was **v2.3.0** (v2.2.9 was also healthy but older).

2. **Rolled back in all regions**
   - Rolled `checkout-api` back to **v2.3.0** across us-east, us-west, and eu-west. The rollback was verified as `rolled_out`.

3. **Opened a SEV2 incident**
   - Created incident **INC-0001** ("checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0"), which paged the on-call engineer, documenting the rollback and the need to investigate the v2.3.1 regression.

4. **Verified recovery**
   - Post-rollback status shows `checkout-api` on **v2.3.0** in all regions, **healthy**, with error rate back down to **0.2%**.

Note: I did not deploy any new version, so no change-manager approval was required — this was a rollback to a previously healthy production release.
